neighbours.label: a manner adverb before a participle describing how something is arranged (neatly folded, tightly packed)
fire: On the bed lay a pile of neatly folded towels.
She handed me a tightly rolled map of the city.
The shelves were full of carefully labelled jars.
He wore a loosely knotted tie to the meeting.
We walked past rows of perfectly trimmed hedges.
The drawer held a stack of crisply pressed napkins.
In the corner sat a box of tightly wrapped presents.
Her hair was pulled back in a neatly braided bun.
quiet: On the bed lay a pile of folded towels.
She handed me an old map of the city.
The shelves were full of labelled glass jars.
He wore a red silk tie to the meeting.
We walked past rows of tall green hedges.
The drawer held a stack of white cotton napkins.
In the corner sat a box of wrapped presents.
Her hair was pulled back in a braided bun.
